- Provide a quarterly evidence bundle for key SOC 2 controls (logs, change management) and a named contact for requests

We also have an internal procurement timeline: procurement aims to complete redlines by 11/15. Happy to take a short call if that helps.

Aisha — thanks for the clear list and the timeline. Looping in Laura from Legal so we can get redlines back quickly. A few quick operational clarifications from our side before legal weighs in:

- SOC2: We run annual Type II audits and can provide our most recent report plus bridge attestation. We can't guarantee a new Type II within 30 days of signature, but we can commit to delivering the latest report and an interim attestation noting the scope; please confirm whether that is acceptable to Zephyr.
- Pen test: By default Redwood prefers a non-production or staging test environment; if a customer needs production testing we require a 30-day notice, scoped test plan, and an agreed blast radius.
- Evidence cadence: We can provide a quarterly evidence package for standard SOC2-relevant artifacts and a named evidence owner.

Laura — I've attached Aisha's questionnaire. Can Legal propose concise MSA appendix language (pen-test notice window, scope carveouts, and evidence turnaround) that we can present to Zephyr?

Next step: Laura/Legal to draft redline language; I'll coordinate a short security call (30m) with Zephyr this week if that helps accelerate.

Subject: Re: Security appendix + SOC2 / pen-test questions for MSA

Aisha — thanks for the questionnaire and timeline. I reviewed the asks and drafted a short appendix and a couple of narrow redlines to the Order Form/Exhibit that should keep the deal moving while protecting both parties. Summary of proposed points (redline attached):

1) SOC 2: Redwood will provide the most recent SOC 2 Type II report and, if requested, a written bridge attestation describing any changes in scope or control status since the report issuance. A representation that a new SOC 2 Type II will be available within 30 days of signature is not something we can accept; we can commit to reasonable cooperation and an attestation.

2) Pen-test / inspection: Customers may request penetration testing. Unless otherwise agreed in writing, penetration testing of production systems requires a minimum 30 calendar days prior written notice, a mutually agreed test plan, and absence of active incident response. Temporary access to a non-production/staging environment is preferred. Redwood will not accept open-ended, unrestricted production testing without scoped limits.

3) Evidence & cadence: Redwood will provide quarterly evidence bundles for SOC 2 controls (log extracts, change control tickets, encryption configuration snapshots) within 10 business days of an evidence request for standard items. For specialized artifacts or forensic logs, Redwood will engage via a documented evidence request ticket and will agree timelines case-by-case.

4) Rollback / remediation language: Proposed mutual language for any disruptive testing activity: the parties will use commercially reasonable efforts to avoid service disruption; if testing causes measurable degradation, Redwood reserves the right to suspend test activity and require remediation/rollback in coordination with customer. We propose an explicit escalation path (named contacts) and an SLA credit framework for remediation-impacting events.

I've attached the redline (ben_redlines_msa.docx). Please review and let us know which items are deal-blockers. If you'd like, Ben and I can join a 30-minute call with your security lead Thursday or Friday.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ben_redlines_msa.docx (docx)

From: Aisha Raymond <aisha@zephyrbio.com>

Subject: Re: Security appendix + SOC2 / pen-test questions for MSA

Laura — appreciate the concise draft. A few clarifications from our procurement/security side after internal review:

> 1) SOC 2: We can accept the "most recent SOC 2 + bridge attestation" approach only if the bridge attestation includes confirmation of control coverage for data retention and access logging for the environment we will use. Can you confirm that the attestation will be scoped to our environment?

> 2) Pen-test notice: Zephyr's policy requires at least 30 calendar days for any production-impacting test. We cannot accept language that allows Redwood to unilaterally suspend test activity without an operational remediation plan; instead we prefer a defined pause-and-restore procedure and a joint incident remediation runbook.

> 3) Evidence cadence: The 10-business-day door for standard items is workable, but procurement wants a firm SLA for turnaround on forensic logs (we ask 5 business days for high-priority event requests). Can Redwood commit to a prioritized evidence track for incidents?

We are not trying to be obstructive — just need these to be clear so legal can sign off. If you can propose specific wording for the attestation scope and the prioritized evidence track, that will speed review. We can do a call Friday 11/06 at 10am PT.

Thanks,
Aisha

Aisha — thanks, and appreciate the specific asks. Below is a compact compromise proposal we can put in the appendix which addresses your procurement constraints while keeping guardrails for Redwood operations. Please review and confirm whether this would be acceptable to Zephyr legal. If yes, Ben will schedule the 30-minute call Friday 11/06 10:00am PT as proposed.

Proposed language (suggested appendix snippets):

- SOC2 Attestation: "Redwood will provide Zephyr with its most recent SOC 2 Type II report and, upon execution, a signed bridge attestation scoped to the production tenant(s) to be used by Zephyr that confirms coverage of access logging and retention controls. For avoidance of doubt, Redwood cannot guarantee issuance of a new SOC2 Type II within 30 days of signature; the bridge attestation is intended to evidence control coverage until the next audit."

- Penetration Testing: "Customer may request penetration testing. For production-impacting tests, the customer must provide at least thirty (30) calendar days prior written notice, a mutually agreed test plan, and agreed rollback procedures. If testing is causing service degradation, the parties will immediately invoke the runbook and the customer shall pause activity upon request while Redwood executes remediation steps. Any suspension will be documented and subject to the remediation SLA described in the appendix."

- Evidence SLA and Prioritization: "Redwood will deliver standard SOC2 evidence artifacts within ten (10) business days of a formal evidence request. For incident-driven forensic requests, Redwood will prioritize such requests and provide a best-effort initial response within five (5) business days, and a target completion timeline to be agreed upon within the ticket. Named evidence owner: security-ops@redwood.com."

If that aligns, we'll produce a clean appendix and redline to incorporate into your draft. Ben — please confirm availability for the 11/06 10am PT call and I'll join.

Thanks,
